Primary request: make a detailed, convincingly dimensional illustration replacing a crude rectangle-and-line backpack-sprayer placeholder. Main composition, upper two-thirds: one unbranded manual backpack agricultural sprayer tank in three-quarter rear-side view, warm pale yellow-green polymer tank with a closed cap, dark padded shoulder straps visible on the tank, a flexible dark hose leading to a slim metal spray lance placed beside the tank. The lance has a straight narrow metal nozzle pipe and a clearly distinct small brass nozzle at its far end. Show the lance completely, not hidden behind the tank, so learners can recognize the pipe separately from the end nozzle. Lower foreground, separate generous whitespace: an enlarged plain black rubber sealing ring and a generic short brass threaded coupling with visibly external threads, as two detached appearance examples, NOT an exploded assembly and NOT shown being installed or matched. Detailed rounded tank form, polymer surface highlights, believable fabric straps, flexible hose material, reflective metal tube and machined brass threads, soft dimensional shadows on warm ivory. Landscape composition with adequate negative space between main equipment and the two enlarged small parts; no panel boxes. No arrows, no text, no labels, no numbers, no logos, no branding, no diagram icons. No liquid, spray mist, operators, hands, chemicals, plants, operation, pressure gauge or certifications. Do not show an internal cutaway, a numbered sequence, exact dimensions, product-specific fittings, or imply the separate ring and coupling are compatible or assembled. The goal is recognizing tank straps, nozzle pipe, nozzle, generic packing ring and a threaded connection; labels will be supplied separately in the app. Do not reproduce any source photograph or illustration.
